svg.title: For every joint input, each partial-trace block for a Hermitian effect perturbation H has trace norm at most ∥H∥∞, by trace-norm duality. The two conclusive blocks and their negative sum give the bound. In the interior regime it is sharp: choose H+ = H−= rI, with null perturbation −2rI. All three blocks are scalar multiples of the reference marginal, giving half trace distance exactly 2r on every input. This is a bound for the declared pointer plus an arbitrary inert reference; it makes no statement about retained output source or bath. For unequal known radii, replace r∥Ay∥1 by ry∥Ay∥1 and 2r by r+ + r−; the analogous margin condition applies. The proof supplies a finite implementation V = P y pEy ⊗|y⟩, retaining the output source and arbitrary inert reference. It demonstrates attainability within ordinary quantum instruments, not a derivation of Born statistics or identity with the physically nominated detector’s full bath.
